headline: Estoril are bottom of the table and still the favourites
summary: Estoril are 18th in the Primeira Liga with 2 points and no win yet, and A Bola reports the club will decide this week whether interim coach Sérgio Raimundo keeps the job. The football explains the price. At Academico Viseu, Estoril made 1.36 expected goals to 0.73 and lost. Moreirense arrive with Maracás out and a new centre-back pairing, which is why, with the bookmakers' margin removed, Estoril are 50.6% favourites against 23.5% — rated 0.5 goals better. The goals line sits at 2.5, with Over at 50.3%.
read: Estoril are bottom of the Primeira Liga with two points from eight games and an interim coach whose future is decided this week, yet the market still makes them 50.6% favourites at home. Moreirense arrive after a 0-1 cup exit with a makeshift centre-back pairing, and the market sees a tight one: the goals line sits at 2.5 and the handicap at half a goal.

facts.fact: Estoril go into the game bottom of the Primeira Liga with two points from eight matches and no win.
facts.meaning: A home game against a mid-table side is exactly the sort of match they need to win, and the table says they have not been winning any of them.

facts.fact: The market still makes bottom-of-the-table Estoril clear favourites at 50.6%, more than twice Moreirense's 23.5%.
facts.meaning: The market weighs this as a home side with the better of the play against a visiting team with defensive problems, not as last versus twelfth.

facts.fact: A Bola reports Estoril's board will decide by Wednesday whether interim coach Sérgio Raimundo keeps the job, with this match described as the real test.
facts.meaning: The home bench is on trial: a result here changes the mood around the club immediately.

facts.fact: Estoril lost 1-2 at Academico Viseu in their last league game despite out-creating their hosts 1.36 to 0.73 on xG.
facts.meaning: They are losing matches they create enough to win, so the problem is converting and defending moments rather than build-up.

facts.fact: Estoril have not beaten Moreirense in their last five meetings — two Moreirense wins and three draws, the latest 1-0 to Moreirense in April.
facts.meaning: This fixture has been tight for two years and Estoril have repeatedly failed to close it out.

facts.fact: The market puts the goals line almost exactly on two and a half, with Over 2.5 at 50.3% and a fair total of 2.51.
facts.meaning: A mid-range, tight game is the expectation — the line sits on the fence rather than pointing to a shootout or a 0-0.

facts.fact: Record reports Moreirense will field a new centre-back pairing of Gilberto Batista alongside Kevyn, with Maracás absent.
facts.meaning: A back line that has not played together is the obvious target for a home side desperate for a win.

facts.fact: A Bola reports that Estoril forward Begraoui picked up a muscle injury during the international break.
facts.meaning: It thins out an attack that has been struggling for goals all season, in a game they are expected to lead.

sources.fact: Portuguese outlet A Bola reports that Estoril's board is increasingly inclined to keep faith with its in-house coach, with the Moreirense match seen as the real test.
OJogo reports that Estoril's SAD will decide by Wednesday whether Sérgio Raimundo is the permanent solution, with several names under consideration for the job.
A Bola reports that Moroccan forward Begraoui has picked up a muscle injury during the international break, raising concern for Estoril.
Estoril confirmed the departure of coach Vasco Matos, with Custódio and João Gião mentioned as possible successors.
Estoril needed penalties to beat lower-league Salgueiros in the Portuguese Cup after a 1-1 score at the end of extra time, having forced the extra period with a goal in the 89th minute.
Correio da Manhã describes Estoril as the last-placed team in the Primeira Liga going into the cup weekend.
Moreirense were eliminated from the Portuguese Cup, losing 1-0 to AVS SAD after Rodrigo Pinho scored the only goal in the 3rd minute.
Moreirense coach Vasco Botelho da Costa said after the cup exit that it may seem almost polemical but he has to be very satisfied with the performance.
